chapter: Jump for Joy, records and royalties
title: Writing songs on the spot; the 1980 Basie session with Eddie Vinson
summary: He lost count of his songs; recently wrote two for Norman Granz at a big-band session with Basie and Vinson.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You have any idea how many numbers you've written?
No. No, indeed. It's hard to keep up with 'em. I done so many numbers. I used to just sit down and make up a song, little no time.
You still do it?

I don't know. I done got kinda lazy on me or forgetful or somethin' here lately. I could sit down now and make up a song. I made up a coupla songs 'bout three...four weeks ago for Norman Granz. Me and Eddie Vinson "Cleanhead" was out there doin' a session with Count Basie so we done a coupla numbers. Then we done a coupla numbers of T-Bone Walker's numbers. And I wrote a couple right there on the spot.
Right there in the studio, huh?
Yeah.
What'd you call them?
"Goin' Away, Baby" and, uh..."How Come My Dog Don't Bark?"
So those will probably be comin' out soon?
Uh huh.
You and Count Basie and "Cleanhead" and...
Eddie Vinson "Cleanhead"...
Reel 2
Uh huh. And is that the session Jake Hanna played drums on?
Huh?
Is that the session that Jake Hanna was the drummer? 'Cause I know Norman was lookin' for Louie Bellson to record somethin' with Basie not long ago, and Louie was out of town...
I don't know who it was.
But I heard he got Jake Hanna in there to play drums.
I didn't know the drummer. In fact, I think they had quite a few new people in his band.
Oh. Oh, it was with the whole Basie band--plus... Ohhh.
Yeah, yeah, we record with whole big band.
Oh. Plus Eddie "Cleanhead" Vinson.
"Jelly Jelly" was with just about six or seven pieces with his band but this time he used the whole big band.
Oh. Oh.
That was somethin' I ain't never done.
You never recorded with the whole band?
Huh uh.
